lines: You have a right to your work,
Do not let the reward be your reason,
and do not cling to doing nothing.

tr: mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi

posts.caption:
Krishna's most quoted line, and the one most of us only read half of.

New here? The Gita is a conversation between Arjuna, a warrior, and Krishna, his charioteer and friend, on the eve of a war. This is the line people quote most.

It says the effort is yours and the result never was. Then it adds the second half: do not hide in doing nothing.

Bhagavad Gita 2.47, on karma.

Which half did you need today? Tell me below.

#bhagavadgita #krishna #karmayoga

slides: You have a right to your work.

The effort is yours. Nobody can take it.

The result depends on a hundred things you don't control.
Do not let the reward be your reason.

Work because it's worth doing. Anything extra is a bonus.

The verse is not permission to quit. It says the opposite.

deck.cover: 5 ways to bring a wandering mind back
deck.sub: Gentle ones. No sitting cross-legged for an hour.
deck.stake: The Gita doesn't say stop the mind from wandering. It says bring it back.
slides: Name it. "Thinking about Monday."
Naming a thought is the first step back.
Look at one thing for ten breaths.
A cup, a leaf, a window. Anything.
Walk slowly, on purpose.
Feel each foot land. Takes two minutes.
Do one thing at a time today.
Eat without the phone. Cook without a podcast.
Forgive the drift and begin again.
6.26: bring it back. That is all of it.
